observed: The owner set the convention for the new dialin package and every package after it: "the new dialin app package would subscribe to the settings app this is project convention from now on and the app we use must be able to still sign it's packages properly where we bring in new features/dependencies and development must be driven in the family byt the cua drivers". Measured against the tree, two gaps existed: the desk carried a private palette/motion table instead of the signed settings document, and the packages loaded assets they never signed (contour.js for dialin, bridge, settings and springboard; phone-calls.js and popit-sw.js for the springboard and the desk), so a new feature could render and be audited without being covered by the package identity.
correction: Two signing-time refusals in app_package.py, checked on the same bytes that are signed: app-not-subscribed (no signed script calls attach("<name>") from /package.js, i.e. the app does not subscribe to the settings app) and app-dependency-undeclared (a served .js/.css the page loads is not in the package's declared files). Every package's file list now declares the assets it loads — contour.js, contour-theme.css, phone-calls.js, popit-sw.js — and was re-signed (dialin@34, bridge@4, settings@23, springboard@32) by the shell publisher with the live driver named. tools/app_package_probe.py proves both refusals with a throwaway surface (16 rows, 0 failed) and the gate carries packages-subscribe-the-settings-app. Development of the packages is driver work: the desk rebuild is wish task-0003, and tools/freshness.py keeps stale packages, tiles, audits, ledgers, refusals, landing and CI rows in front of the drivers with the act that clears each one.
